headline: This change publishes a live payment key in the code and makes test previews charge real cards.
what_changed: A new settings file holding the live payment keys for the website is added to the project.
The project rule that kept settings files out of the shared code is removed, so such files can now be uploaded.
The payment code now uses the live payment account whenever the setting is missing, such as on preview versions of the site.
The stated reason is that preview versions were failing at checkout. Any checkout on those versions now takes real money from real cards.

risks.title: Live payment secret key saved in the project files
risks.explanation: The live secret key is written into a settings file that is no longer excluded from the shared code. Anyone who can see the code could use it to make charges, issue refunds, and view customer payment records. Deleting the file would not remove the key from the project history, so the key should be treated as exposed. It should be cancelled in the payment dashboard, replaced with a new one, and set only in the hosting settings.

risks.title: Test and preview sites will charge real customers' cards
risks.explanation: If the setting is missing, the payment code now falls back to the live account. Preview sites can be reached by staff and testers, and any checkout there creates a real charge. This fallback also keeps the live key in the code even if the setting is added later. Remove the fallback and set a separate test key for preview sites.

risks.title: Removed safety rule makes future secret leaks easier
risks.explanation: The rule that stopped settings files from being shared is removed. Future settings files containing passwords or keys could be uploaded by accident. Restoring the rule would prevent this and keep the example settings file shareable.

questions_for_developer: Has the live payment secret key already been pushed to a shared repository? If yes, has it been cancelled in the payment dashboard and replaced?
Why do preview versions of the site not have the payment setting? Can a test-mode key be added to the hosting settings for previews instead?
Can the fallback to the live key be removed, so the site stops with a clear error when the setting is missing rather than charging real cards?
Can the settings file be removed from this change and the old sharing rule restored?
good_news: The change touches only three files, so reverting it is quick and simple.
The live publishable key is meant to be visible in the website, so that part is less serious than the secret key.
